counterexample: Take Xi = {P1E,P2E,P1C,P2C} and sigma = {P1E,P2E}^omega. Then sigma does not satisfy G((P1E&P2E) -> F(P1C|P2C)), and the step-0016 recipe picks i=0 with hat-sigma = sigma[..0] = {P1E,P2E}. But the extension sigma' = {P1E,P2E}.{P1C}.(empty)^omega has hat-sigma as a prefix and DOES satisfy the formula: at position 0 the antecedent holds but F(P1C|P2C) holds too (P1C at position 1), and at every position >= 1 the antecedent P1E&P2E is false. So P_safe intersected with the cylinder of hat-sigma is nonempty, i.e. hat-sigma is not a bad prefix. The same holds for every finite prefix of sigma (always extendable by a P1C letter), so sigma has NO bad prefix at all and the safety definition of steps 0010-0012 fails. Indeed the property is liveness (steps 0024-0034 prove pref(P) = (2^Xi)*), and it is not (2^Xi)^omega since sigma above is excluded, so it cannot also be safety.

0016 - FAILS. The opening is fine: if sigma does not satisfy G(phi) then some i >= 0 has sigma,i not satisfying phi = (P1E&P2E) -> F(P1C|P2C). But the two subsequent assertions are unjustified and false. (a) 'hat-sigma = sigma[..i] is a bad prefix' is merely asserted. (b) The inference 'for any sigma' extending hat-sigma, sigma',i does not satisfy phi' is invalid: sigma,i not satisfying phi means sigma,i |= P1E&P2E AND sigma,i does not satisfy F(P1C|P2C). The first conjunct is determined by position i and is indeed inherited by any extension of sigma[..i]; the second conjunct is NOT prefix-determined - F(P1C|P2C) at position i quantifies over all positions j >= i, i.e. over the whole infinite suffix, which the prefix sigma[..i] does not constrain. An extension sigma' that places P1C at some position j > i satisfies F(P1C|P2C) at i and hence satisfies phi at i. The argument silently treats a formula containing an unbounded eventuality as if it were a state formula evaluable from the prefix; the identical reasoning would 'prove' that G(F p) is a safety property, which is false. No bad prefix exists for this property (see counterexample field).
